title: Cap a cocktail shaker and shake it on its side without spilling
instruction: Put the cap on the shaker tin and shake the shaker on its side, back and forth along its length, with the cap kept seated on the tin the whole time it is tipped; then stand it back upright on the table without losing any of the beads.
context: Bartenders cap a shaker tin and shake it with both hands: a cap that is not held on lifts and sprays the drink, and one hand cannot both keep the cap on and swing the tin. The same close, hold and agitate motion is used to mix capped flasks and bottles in labs and kitchens.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) An open steel shaker tin, 19 cm tall, 7.6 cm across outside (7.0 cm inside), with a 3 mm wall and a 5 mm floor, 0.20 kg, loose, standing upright on the centre line 22 cm forward. (2) Its steel cap, 0.08 kg, loose: a top disc 9 cm across and 4 mm thick; under it a skirt 1.5 cm deep and 3 mm thick that clears the tin by 4 mm at the disc and flares out to 9 mm at its lower edge; on top a square knob 2.2 cm front to back, 3 cm side to side and 5.2 cm tall. The cap rests on (3) a fixed dark grey post 4 cm across and 19 cm tall, 33 cm forward and 5 cm right of the centre line. (4) The drink and ice: 12 red plastic beads 6 mm across, 0.8 g each, lying on the tin's floor. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. A bead is kept while its centre is inside the tin or inside the cap's skirt. 0.0 unless the tin ends standing on the table (tilted less than 10 degrees). Tipping and shaking count only while the shaker is capped and held: the cap seated on the tin (its disc's centre within 8 mm of the tin's axis and of its rim, its axis within 12 degrees of the tin's) with a gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of the cap's knob; in a real trial, judged from the video as the cap sitting fully on the tin with a gripper on it. Otherwise 1.0 if the capped and held tin was at some point tipped 80 degrees or more from upright and, while tipped more than 60 degrees, was shaken back and forth along its own axis (its middle moving 2 cm or more one way, then 2 cm or more back, at least 4 changes of direction), with all 12 beads kept; 0.5 if so shaken with at most 2 beads lost; 0.25 if tipped 80 degrees or more but shaken less, with all 12 beads kept; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: put the beads back in the tin, stand the tin on its spot and set the cap back on its post, knob up.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the drink and ice are 12 rigid 6 mm beads (they rattle and spill but do not slosh); the cap is a loose fit with no seal, so it stays on only while pressed; the tin's wall is 20 flat panels, the skirt 24; friction is set (tin and cap 0.7, beads 0.3); the cameras render at 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
